question.title: proposal: Go 2: Array or variadic destructuring to discrete variables
question.caller: A Go developer processing optional heterogeneous arguments in NewExtParam(value interface{}, opts ...interface{}).
question.input: An array or variadic sequence; concrete initial example is opts ...interface{}, plus an ordered list of destination variables.
question.output: Separate destination variables receive available sequence values from left to right; destinations past the input length receive a null/nil value.
limits: Only the initial heterogeneous options example and stated array/variadic boundary are fixed. The text does not resolve the static type of a missing value for every possible typed array.
Extra source elements do not require extra destinations; only specified destinations are assigned.
The long strconv/type-switch example illustrates existing caller processing, not a requirement that the supplier perform numeric parsing.
No speed target, concurrency guarantee, general pattern matching or generics requirement is supplied.

source_sections.heading: Proposal: requested assignment and existing processing example
Costs and named PHP list analogy

whole_must.requirement: Provide a Go-level array/variadic destructuring assignment that binds separate destination variables without caller-written per-element length/index checks.
whole_must.falsifying_input: In a Go function with opts=[]interface{}{7,"x"}, attempting a three-variable destructuring still requires the caller to implement len(opts) checks and opts[i] extraction.
whole_must.predicate: Provide a Go-level array/variadic destructuring assignment that binds separate destination variables without caller-written per-element length/index checks.

whole_must.requirement: Assign the supplied destinations in left-to-right source order, and do not require more destinations than the caller specified.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10,20,30] with two destinations produces (20,10), rejects the unused third value, or requires a third destination.
whole_must.predicate: Assign the supplied destinations in left-to-right source order, and do not require more destinations than the caller specified.

whole_must.requirement: For the heterogeneous options boundary, produce nil/null for a destination beyond the source length so the caller can test it.
whole_must.falsifying_input: Input [10] with three interface-valued destinations panics, rejects the arity mismatch, or yields non-null fabricated values in positions two and three.
whole_must.predicate: For the heterogeneous options boundary, produce nil/null for a destination beyond the source length so the caller can test it.

partial_must.requirement: Extract an ordered fixed-width group of values from an array/variadic-like sequence without the caller implementing individual element extraction.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For [10,20,30] and width two, the component only exposes raw indexing and requires the adapter to implement the extraction loop.
partial_must.predicate: Extract an ordered fixed-width group of values from an array/variadic-like sequence without the caller implementing individual element extraction.

partial_must.requirement: Preserve left-to-right values, truncate unused trailing source positions, and pad missing heterogeneous positions with null/nil.
partial_must.falsifying_input: For input [10] and width three the result is not (10,null,null), or for [10,20,30] and width two it rejects rather than returning the first two values.
partial_must.predicate: Preserve left-to-right values, truncate unused trailing source positions, and pad missing heterogeneous positions with null/nil.

question.independent_partial_purpose: Prepare a fixed-width, null-padded tuple of optional argument values for validation before Go language syntax is integrated.
question.independently_useful_next_action: The caller can check the three extracted option positions for nil and perform the existing per-type processing.
question.remaining_adapter: Bind the prepared positions to Go variables and integrate any new compiler syntax/type rules; retain caller-specific numeric/type conversions. An adapter that implements sequence extraction or missing-value padding itself does not establish partial completion.
preferences: The example syntax is sz, sc, pr := opts...; punctuation is an illustrated syntax preference, while the assignment semantics are mandatory.
Less code clutter and easier understanding are motivations, not measured performance predicates.

named_component_roles.PHP list: Explicit existing analogy for the same value-retrieval use; rediscovery is not a new target.
named_component_roles.strconv.ParseInt: Existing downstream type conversion, outside the destructuring action.

question.same_name_wrong_actor_output_failure: A list API that appends values, enumerates variable names, or returns a string representation does not perform ordered destructuring with missing-position nulls, even if it is named list/unpack.
